=== Dungeon Dare ===

Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

COMPONENTS. A monster deck of 13 cards (name: strength): Goblin 1 (x2), Skeleton 2 (x2), Orc 3 (x2), Vampire 4 (x2), Golem 5 (x2), Lich 6 (x1), Demon 7 (x1), Dragon 9 (x1). The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.
(f) If exactly one player is still IN, that player is the RUNNER and the run happens now. Otherwise the turn passes to the next IN player.

THE RUN. The runner's HP is 3, +4 if ARMOR remains, +3 if SHIELD remains. Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

END OF GAME. After any run, if any player has 4 or more points, the game ends. The game also ends after turn 40, even mid-dungeon; an unfinished dungeon is not scored. The player with the most points wins; players tied for the most share the result (a draw).

- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.
(f) If exactly one player is still IN, that player is the RUNNER and the run happens now. Otherwise the turn passes to the next IN player.

Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

END OF GAME. After any run, if any player has 4 or more points, the game ends. The game also ends after turn 40, even mid-dungeon; an unfinished dungeon is not scored. The player with the most points wins; players tied for the most share the result (a draw).

The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. (b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. - ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.
(f) If exactly one player is still IN, that player is the RUNNER and the run happens now. Otherwise the turn passes to the next IN player.

Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.

A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Dungeon Dare ===

Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

COMPONENTS. A monster deck of 13 cards (name: strength): Goblin 1 (x2), Skeleton 2 (x2), Orc 3 (x2), Vampire 4 (x2), Golem 5 (x2), Lich 6 (x1), Demon 7 (x1), Dragon 9 (x1). The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.
(f) If exactly one player is still IN, that player is the RUNNER and the run happens now. Otherwise the turn passes to the next IN player.

THE RUN. The runner's HP is 3, +4 if ARMOR remains, +3 if SHIELD remains. Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

END OF GAME. After any run, if any player has 4 or more points, the game ends. The game also ends after turn 40, even mid-dungeon; an unfinished dungeon is not scored. The player with the most points wins; players tied for the most share the result (a draw).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.

[user]
=== Dungeon Dare ===

Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

COMPONENTS. A monster deck of 13 cards (name: strength): Goblin 1 (x2), Skeleton 2 (x2), Orc 3 (x2), Vampire 4 (x2), Golem 5 (x2), Lich 6 (x1), Demon 7 (x1), Dragon 9 (x1). The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.
(f) If exactly one player is still IN, that player is the RUNNER and the run happens now. Otherwise the turn passes to the next IN player.

THE RUN. The runner's HP is 3, +4 if ARMOR remains, +3 if SHIELD remains. Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

END OF GAME. After any run, if any player has 4 or more points, the game ends. The game also ends after turn 40, even mid-dungeon; an unfinished dungeon is not scored. The player with the most points wins; players tied for the most share the result (a draw).

Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.
(f) If exactly one player is still IN, that player is the RUNNER and the run happens now. Otherwise the turn passes to the next IN player.

THE RUN. The runner's HP is 3, +4 if ARMOR remains, +3 if SHIELD remains. Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

END OF GAME. After any run, if any player has 4 or more points, the game ends. The game also ends after turn 40, even mid-dungeon; an unfinished dungeon is not scored. The player with the most points wins; players tied for the most share the result (a draw).

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Dungeon Dare ===

Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

COMPONENTS. A monster deck of 13 cards (name: strength): Goblin 1 (x2), Skeleton 2 (x2), Orc 3 (x2), Vampire 4 (x2), Golem 5 (x2), Lich 6 (x1), Demon 7 (x1), Dragon 9 (x1). The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.

=== Dungeon Dare ===

Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

COMPONENTS. A monster deck of 13 cards (name: strength): Goblin 1 (x2), Skeleton 2 (x2), Orc 3 (x2), Vampire 4 (x2), Golem 5 (x2), Lich 6 (x1), Demon 7 (x1), Dragon 9 (x1). The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.

Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.

Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

END OF GAME. After any run, if any player has 4 or more points, the game ends. The game also ends after turn 40, even mid-dungeon; an unfinished dungeon is not scored. The player with the most points wins; players tied for the most share the result (a draw).

=== Dungeon Dare ===

Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

COMPONENTS. A monster deck of 13 cards (name: strength): Goblin 1 (x2), Skeleton 2 (x2), Orc 3 (x2), Vampire 4 (x2), Golem 5 (x2), Lich 6 (x1), Demon 7 (x1), Dragon 9 (x1). The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.
(f) If exactly one player is still IN, that player is the RUNNER and the run happens now. Otherwise the turn passes to the next IN player.

THE RUN. The runner's HP is 3, +4 if ARMOR remains, +3 if SHIELD remains. Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

END OF GAME. After any run, if any player has 4 or more points, the game ends. The game also ends after turn 40, even mid-dungeon; an unfinished dungeon is not scored. The player with the most points wins; players tied for the most share the result (a draw).

records.system: You are one player in a game on the XColos platform, played by turns. You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. Think about the rules, the other players and what they have done, then act. When you are asked to act, reply with exactly one legal answer in the form the question asks for, and keep any reasoning short and before the answer. Do not ask questions back.

[user]
=== Dungeon Dare ===

Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

COMPONENTS. A monster deck of 13 cards (name: strength): Goblin 1 (x2), Skeleton 2 (x2), Orc 3 (x2), Vampire 4 (x2), Golem 5 (x2), Lich 6 (x1), Demon 7 (x1), Dragon 9 (x1). The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.
(f) If exactly one player is still IN, that player is the RUNNER and the run happens now. Otherwise the turn passes to the next IN player.

THE RUN. The runner's HP is 3, +4 if ARMOR remains, +3 if SHIELD remains. Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

END OF GAME. After any run, if any player has 4 or more points, the game ends. The game also ends after turn 40, even mid-dungeon; an unfinished dungeon is not scored. The player with the most points wins; players tied for the most share the result (a draw).

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Dungeon Dare ===

Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

COMPONENTS. A monster deck of 13 cards (name: strength): Goblin 1 (x2), Skeleton 2 (x2), Orc 3 (x2), Vampire 4 (x2), Golem 5 (x2), Lich 6 (x1), Demon 7 (x1), Dragon 9 (x1). The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).

(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.

- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. records.prompt:
[user]
=== Dungeon Dare ===

Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

COMPONENTS. A monster deck of 13 cards (name: strength): Goblin 1 (x2), Skeleton 2 (x2), Orc 3 (x2), Vampire 4 (x2), Golem 5 (x2), Lich 6 (x1), Demon 7 (x1), Dragon 9 (x1). The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.
(f) If exactly one player is still IN, that player is the RUNNER and the run happens now. Otherwise the turn passes to the next IN player.

THE RUN. The runner's HP is 3, +4 if ARMOR remains, +3 if SHIELD remains. Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

END OF GAME. After any run, if any player has 4 or more points, the game ends. The game also ends after turn 40, even mid-dungeon; an unfinished dungeon is not scored. The player with the most points wins; players tied for the most share the result (a draw).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 3. Seats are numbered 1 to 3.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Dungeon Dare ===

Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

COMPONENTS. A monster deck of 13 cards (name: strength): Goblin 1 (x2), Skeleton 2 (x2), Orc 3 (x2), Vampire 4 (x2), Golem 5 (x2), Lich 6 (x1), Demon 7 (x1), Dragon 9 (x1). The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
Dungeon Dare, for 3 players (seats 1, 2 and 3). Everyone starts with 0 points.

COMPONENTS. A monster deck of 13 cards (name: strength): Goblin 1 (x2), Skeleton 2 (x2), Orc 3 (x2), Vampire 4 (x2), Golem 5 (x2), Lich 6 (x1), Demon 7 (x1), Dragon 9 (x1). The adventurer has base HP 3 and 4 items: ARMOR (+4 HP), SHIELD (+3 HP), TORCH (defeats every monster of strength 3 or less), SPEAR (defeats every monster of strength 7 or more).

STARTING A DUNGEON. The game is a series of turns, at most 40, grouped into dungeons. At the start of each dungeon all 13 monsters are shuffled into a face-down deck (the only random event), all 4 items return to the adventurer, the dungeon pile and all set-aside piles are emptied, all three players are IN, and every 'added' mark is cleared. Dungeon 1 is led by seat 1, dungeon 2 by seat 2, dungeon 3 by seat 3, dungeon 4 by seat 1, and so on. The leader acts first; turns then pass in seat order (1, 2, 3, 1, ...), skipping players who are OUT.

A TURN (for the active player, who is IN).
(a) Forced pass: if the deck holds 2 or fewer cards, the active player draws nothing, there is no talk, and PASS is the only option.
(b) Draw: otherwise the active player privately looks at the top card of the deck. Only they see it.
(c) Talk: every player, IN or OUT, writes one short message at the same time; then all messages are shown to everyone. Messages bind no one and may be lies.
(d) Action: the active player chooses one of the legal options, in this order:
- PASS: you become OUT for this dungeon. The card you drew, if any, goes back on top of the deck, unseen by others.
- ADD: put the drawn monster face-down on the dungeon pile, and you are marked 'added' for this dungeon.
- SACRIFICE_ARMOR, SACRIFICE_SHIELD, SACRIFICE_TORCH, SACRIFICE_SPEAR: offered only for items still present. That item is removed from the adventurer for this dungeon, and the drawn monster goes face-down to your own set-aside pile, out of play and seen only by you. This does NOT mark you as 'added'. An item already removed this dungeon is not offered.
(e) Announcement: everyone learns the option chosen, which item was removed if any, and how many cards are in the dungeon pile (0 now). Nobody learns which monster was drawn.
(f) If exactly one player is still IN, that player is the RUNNER and the run happens now. Otherwise the turn passes to the next IN player.

THE RUN. The runner's HP is 3, +4 if ARMOR remains, +3 if SHIELD remains. Every card in the dungeon pile is revealed, then the top 2 cards of the deck; these are all the monsters faced, and all are announced. A monster is defeated with no damage if TORCH remains and its strength is 3 or less, or if SPEAR remains and its strength is 7 or more; otherwise it deals damage equal to its strength. If total damage is less than HP, the run SUCCEEDS and the runner gains 2 points (OUT players gain nothing). Otherwise the run FAILS: the runner loses 1 point (never below 0), and every OUT player marked 'added' for this dungeon gains 1 point. Either way the dungeon ends and the next turn starts a new dungeon.

END OF GAME. After any run, if any player has 4 or more points, the game ends. The game also ends after turn 40, even mid-dungeon; an unfinished dungeon is not scored. The player with the most points wins; players tied for the most share the result (a draw).
